test_title: PYST 19: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I - GA (Held On: 13 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: With reference to the 40th Amendment Act, 1976, which category of maritime zones came under the legislative jurisdiction of the Parliament?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Territorial waters and EEZ**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 40th Amendment Act, 1976, brought **Territorial waters, Continental Shelf, Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ), and other maritime zones** under the legislative jurisdiction of the Parliament.
 
• This amendment added **Entry 25 to the Union List** in the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India, empowering Parliament to legislate on these areas.
 
• The aim was to align India's constitutional framework with **international maritime laws**, specifically the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS).
 
• The amendment reinforced India's **sovereign rights** over resources in these maritime zones, including fisheries, oil, and natural gas exploration.
 
• This was a crucial step in establishing a clear legal framework for India's maritime boundaries and jurisdiction over its waters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Territorial Waters:**

 
 
• Territorial waters extend up to **12 nautical miles** from the baseline of a coastal state.
 
• The state has **sovereignty** over these waters, including the airspace above and the seabed below.
 
 
 
• **Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ):**
 
 
• The EEZ extends up to **200 nautical miles** from the baseline.
 
• In this zone, the coastal state has **special rights** regarding the exploration and use of marine resources, including energy production from water and wind.
 
 
 
• **Continental Shelf:**
 
 
• The continental shelf is the seabed and subsoil that extends beyond the territorial waters, up to **200 nautical miles** or more, depending on geological criteria.
 
• The coastal state has sovereign rights for exploring and exploiting natural resources in this area.
 
 
 
• **United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS):**
 
 
• UNCLOS, also known as the **Law of the Sea Treaty**, was adopted in **1982**.
 
• It defines maritime zones such as territorial waters, EEZ, and continental shelf and establishes the rights and responsibilities of nations regarding the use of oceans.
 
 
 
• **India's Maritime Claims:**
 
 
• India has a coastline of approximately **11,084** **km** and an EEZ of **2.37 million square kilometers**.
 
• The legislative jurisdiction over maritime zones enables India to safeguard its strategic, economic, and environmental interests.
